    {"name": "mentions_b2b", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Useful business-model axis; sampled values consistent with text."},
    {"name": "mentions_b2c", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Useful business-model axis; consistent with sampled text."},
    {"name": "has_funding_language", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Reasonable flag; 5AM Ventures 'returns to investors' correctly flagged; others correctly 0."},
    {"name": "action_verb_score", "analytical_usefulness": 0.3, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Generic stylistic/marketing-tone feature with weak connection to regional cluster; values derivable from text."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
  "source_groundedness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "The set mixes genuinely useful categorical/industry features (primary_industry, is_* flags, mentions_b2b/b2c, has_funding_language) that offer real axes for grouping and modeling, with several low-leverage surface/stylometric features (word count, avg word length, sentence count, action_verb_score) that add little for this query. Groundedness is generally decent for extractive flags, but the industry tagging over-fires—especially is_ai_ml (fired for 23andme and 280 Group without textual support) and industry_tag_count inheriting these spurious tags—and treatment of VC firms (5AM Ventures, Accel) is inconsistent (life-science VC labeled both fintech and healthcare and enterprise_sw). These represent confident specifics not warranted by the text, lowering the source-groundedness verdict."
